name: Chicken Parmesan
description: The Italian-American red-sauce classic: thin chicken cutlets breaded with Parmigiano and breadcrumbs, shallow-fried until crisp, then topped with a quick marinara and melted mozzarella and broiled until bubbling. Serves 4.

ingredients.text: 800 g canned whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
ingredients.item: canned whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand

ingredients.text: 6 basil leaves, plus more to serve
ingredients.item: basil leaves, plus more to serve

ingredients.text: 2 large boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 700 g)
ingredients.item: large boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 700 g)

ingredients.text: 30 g Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated (for the breading)

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp olive oil (for the sauce) with 3 garlic cloves, thinly sliced and 1/4 tsp red chili flakes in a saucepan over medium for 2 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold. Add 800 g canned whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand, 1/2 tsp salt (for the sauce) and 6 basil leaves, plus more to serve and simmer 20 minutes, until thickened.
Halve 2 large boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 700 g) horizontally into 4 cutlets and pound to an even 1 cm. Season with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper.

Set up 60 g all-purpose flour, 2 eggs, beaten, and 100 g dried breadcrumbs or panko mixed with 30 g Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated (for the breading) in three shallow dishes. Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then the crumbs, pressing to adhere.
Heat 240 ml neutral oil (for frying) in a large skillet over medium-high to 175°C. Fry the cutlets 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack.

Heat the broiler. Arrange the cutlets on a sheet pan, spoon a stripe of sauce down the center of each (leaving the edges crisp), and top with 225 g low-moisture mozzarella, grated and 30 g Parmigiano-Reggiano, grated.
Broil 3 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots. Serve with basil, the rest of the sauce, and 400 g spaghetti, cooked (optional, to serve).

notes: Leaving some crust uncovered by sauce keeps the cutlets crisp. Low-moisture mozzarella browns and doesn't weep like fresh. Leftovers make an excellent chicken parm sandwich on a hero roll.
